steps: In dynamic equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates, so the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant.
In static equilibrium, no reaction or movement takes place; the system is at rest.
items.finalAnswer: Dynamic equilibrium has continuing reactions at equal rates, whereas static equilibrium has no reaction or movement.

steps: The decomposition of water into hydrogen and oxygen is an endothermic reaction.
According to Le Chatelier’s principle, increasing the temperature favours the endothermic direction.
Therefore, the equilibrium shifts to the right and the yield of hydrogen and oxygen increases.
items.finalAnswer: Increasing the temperature shifts the equilibrium to the right, increasing the yield of hydrogen and oxygen.

steps: The yield of products can be increased by changing the conditions to favour the forward reaction.
Choose a suitable temperature and pressure according to the heat change and the number of gaseous molecules in the reaction.
Remove the products as they form, where possible, to shift the equilibrium towards the products.
items.finalAnswer: Use conditions that favour the forward reaction and remove products as they form.

steps: Add a suitable catalyst to the reaction mixture.
A catalyst increases the rates of both the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached sooner.
A catalyst does not change the position of equilibrium.
items.finalAnswer: A suitable catalyst decreases the time required to attain equilibrium.

steps: There are two moles of gaseous reactants and two moles of gaseous products.
An increase in pressure does not favour either side when the number of gaseous molecules is equal on both sides.
Therefore, the equilibrium position does not change.
items.finalAnswer: Increasing the pressure has no effect on the equilibrium position.

steps: A reversible reaction can proceed in both forward and reverse directions because its products can react to form the original reactants under the same conditions.
An irreversible reaction proceeds mainly in one direction because its products do not readily react to form the original reactants under the same conditions.
items.finalAnswer: Reactions differ in reversibility because their products differ in their ability to form the original reactants under the same conditions.

steps: Combustion reactions are generally highly exothermic.
Their products are stable and do not readily react to form the original substances under ordinary conditions.
Therefore, combustion reactions proceed mainly in the forward direction and are generally irreversible.
items.finalAnswer: Combustion reactions are generally irreversible because they release much heat and their stable products do not readily reform the reactants.

steps: A reversible reaction can be made to proceed practically in one direction by continuously removing one of its products.
An apparently irreversible reaction may be reversed if suitable conditions are provided for its products to react back.
Thus, reversibility depends on the reaction conditions; not every irreversible reaction can be reversed.
items.finalAnswer: Changing conditions can make a reversible reaction proceed one way, and may reverse an apparently irreversible reaction when suitable conditions allow.
